newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares stage weak rebound, seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares stage weak rebound, seen falling.

text.p: Polish shares rebounded in higher trade on Tuesday after a three-session fall but analysts said the small scale of the rise and strong selling after price fixing indicated the market's weakness and suggested falls.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 64.9 points or 0.4 percent to 14,958.3, and turnover rose 9.2 percent to 122.5 million zlotys ($43.8 million) on both markets as 46 issues rose, 15 fell and 19 were flat.
"It's clear the market is loosing strength as heavy supply turned up immediately after today's slight rebound," said Emil Onyszczuk, a trader at Polish Development Bank (PBR) brokerage.

Analysts said the market looked too weak to beat the October 9 high at 15,078.7 points of the WIG index this week, as they expected earlier, and said the weakness was due to the market's 100-percent growth since the beginning of 1996.

They said Tuesday's news Polish consumer prices rose 1.9 percent in September, bringing year-on-year inflation down to 19.5 percent was unlikely to influence the market as it had not expected a rate-cut before the year's end anyway.
They also said the market was likely to experience speculative play on selected stocks ahead of companies monthly earnings reports for September, due later this week.

Construction firm Mostostal Zabrze plunged 9.3 percent in 0.4-million-zloty turnover ($0.1 million) on a court decision to halt its 25-million-zloty ($8.9 million) contract to build a radio and TV mast.
Mass privatisation NFI units fell 6.1 percent in a 22.6-million zloty turnover ($8.1 million) in regular session and 6.0 percent in 19.8-million zloty ($7.1 million) continuous trade.
